results.title: Within hangs: how long does the vendor's tool wait, call after call?
results.basis: README: telemetry is added around the vendor's tool; the vendor's result should not depend on Within answering.
results.observed: five calls with Within never answering took 2, 0, 0, 0, 0 ms. Worst 2 ms.

results.title: Within hangs for a while, then recovers: does telemetry resume without a restart?
results.basis: Vendor expectation. The SDK's own send code sets no timeout and runs at most 5 requests at once.
results.observed: Within hung on 5 requests, then answered normally. In the next 15 s after recovery, requests reaching Within: 0 (3 later reports were waiting). The vendor's own calls stayed fast. The SDK code sets no timeout on these requests, so the stuck requests keep every later event waiting. I did not wait for Node's own default limit to see when they give up.

results.title: A long free-text argument: does redaction freeze the vendor's whole process? (event-loop stall, 4 sizes, 2 shapes)
results.basis: README: 'Configurable field and event limits truncate oversized payloads' (default 10,000 bytes per field). Vendor expectation: the SDK runs inside the vendor's process.
results.observed: event-loop stall per argument (ms): letters 10000 chars -> 109; letters 25000 chars -> 334; letters 50000 chars -> 1882; letters 100000 chars -> 6252; words 100000 chars -> 17; dots 50000 chars -> 1384. The vendor's own tool call returned in about 2 ms each time: the freeze comes after, while the event is cleaned, and blocks every customer on the process. Cause: the email pattern in privacy.js is applied to the whole string before it is cut to the 10,000-byte limit.

results.title: Does loading the SDK change how the vendor's process handles SIGTERM? (one signal, then a second one 3 s later)
results.basis: Source: eventQueue.js registers process.once handlers for SIGINT, SIGTERM and beforeExit.
results.observed: SIGTERM to a plain Node process: exited after 2 ms. To a process that called track(): still running after 12 s (force-killed). With a second SIGTERM sent 3 s after the first: exited after 3003 ms (signal SIGTERM).

results.title: The email pattern on its own: time against input length (copy of the pattern, checked against the package file)
results.basis: Isolates the cause of the freeze measured in C8.
results.observed: pattern found in privacy.js unchanged: true. Letters with no @ (ms): 10000 -> 55, 25000 -> 358, 50000 -> 1463, 100000 -> 5879. Doubling the length multiplied the time by about 4.0. Ordinary words (100,000 chars): 1 ms. The same 100,000 letters cut to 10,000 first: 60 ms. An email in 100,000 spaces: 0 ms.
